title: Marty McFly's watch: what most fans get wrong

slides.title: Most fans get Marty's watch *wrong.*
slides.body: Everyone “knows” Marty McFly wears a Casio CA-53W. In the 1985 original, he doesn't.

slides.title: A very *80s* gadget
slides.body: Calculator watches are peak tech: a tiny keypad, a digital display, **a computer on your wrist.** The perfect watch for a teenager whose best friend is a mad scientist.

slides.title: Meet the *CA-50*
slides.body: In the first film, Marty wears a **Casio CA-50** calculator watch. In 1988 Casio replaced it with a successor, and the two got mixed up for good.

slides.title: Enter the *CA-53W*
slides.body: In Part II (1989) and Part III (1990), Marty wears the **CA-53W** (right). That's the one fans remember, and it's still on sale.

image.credit: Left CA-50, right CA-53W · Photo: VSchagow · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

slides.title: The film opens with *clocks*
slides.body: A wall of ticking clocks, all set **exactly 25 minutes slow** by Doc's experiment. That's why Marty is late for school.

slides.title: The most famous *stopped clock*
slides.body: On November 12, 1955, lightning strikes the Hill Valley clock tower and **stops it at 10:04 p.m.** Doc uses that bolt to send Marty home.

slides.title: Casio *goes back*
slides.body: For the film's 40th anniversary, Casio releases the **CA-500WEBF**, with a dial inspired by the DeLorean's OUTATIME plate and keys inspired by the time circuits.

slides.title: Where we're going, we still need *watches.*
slides.next: Why watch ads show 10:10, and why our clock shows 10:04

caption:
Quick test for Back to the Future fans: which Casio does Marty wear? ⌚⚡

Most people say CA-53W, but in the 1985 original it's the CA-50. The CA-53W only appears in Part II and Part III. And in 2025, for the film's 40th anniversary, Casio released a special calculator watch inspired by the DeLorean.

Did you know? Be honest 👇

Sources: Wikipedia (Casio CA-53W); Casio; the film.
